  4. See the vertex, axis of symmetry and factored form too.

❓ Frequently asked questions

What does the discriminant tell me?

The discriminant D = b²−4ac. D > 0 means two distinct real roots, D = 0 one repeated root, D < 0 two complex conjugate roots.

What if a is zero?

Then it is not quadratic — it is the linear equation bx+c=0. The tool rejects a=0 instead of solving the wrong equation.

How are complex roots shown?

As a±bi, the standard complex form, computed from the real part −b/2a and imaginary part √|D|/2a.
